findings.title: Recovery proposals execute without Trust Gateway reevaluation
findings.evidence: execute_step evaluates original proposal at 208-213, but recovery_fixer returns a new proposal at 304 and sandbox_runner(fixed_proposal) runs at 311 without evaluate or replay check.
findings.trigger: An admitted action fails and recovery_fixer changes the target to a sensitive path, tool, or previously failed action.
findings.impact: The callback receives the changed action without the deterministic rejection applied to normal actions; record_step_atomic then records ADMIT if it succeeds. Scope is this executor callback boundary, not proof of an OS sandbox escape.

findings.title: Required structured review is only a quota counter
findings.evidence: Lines 255-258 spend recovery quota and set structured_review_used=True; line 260 unconditionally calls sandbox_runner. No review callable, review output, or approval decision exists.
findings.trigger: An irreversible/architectural proposal requires review, including when recovery quota is exhausted.
findings.impact: The action executes without the required independent review, and successful events may report structured_review=True despite no review being performed.

findings.title: Completion endpoint returns canned legal output as model inference
findings.evidence: Lines 146-198 choose format! strings based on model ID; gguf_model is only read for tensor_count at 144. The reply at 212-232 labels the response with the requested model and generated token usage.
findings.trigger: Any POST to /v1/chat/completions, including with missing/unloadable GGUF or an unrelated question.
findings.impact: Clients receive fixed legal conclusions and attested-success text rather than inference from the advertised model; conversation history other than the final content is ignored.

findings.title: WebSocket and completion routes never invoke the instantiated authentication validator
findings.evidence: create_router installs routes without authentication middleware (53-62); ws_handler discards AppState (238), and handle_socket acknowledges channels/RPC at 249-264 without credentials. chat_completions_handler likewise has no authentication extractor/check. main.rs 44-48 and 59-80 serves this router locally.
findings.trigger: A local process connects to /ws or POSTs completions without supplying the dual passkey.
findings.impact: The configured DualPasskeyAuth is unused; untrusted local clients can invoke these operations and obtain receipts. This is a localhost authorization gap, not remote network exposure.

findings.title: Snapshot engine resolves its root above the repository
findings.evidence: REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).parent.parents[2]; for repo/scripts/c5_l1_ledger/ledger_snapshot_engine.py this is the repository parent. DB_PATH and SNAPSHOT_DIR derive from it at 25-26.
findings.trigger: Run the script from its checked-in location without monkeypatching globals.
findings.impact: It reads or creates the parent directory cortex.db and writes snapshots outside this repository, rather than backing up this repository cortex.db; the missing-source branch can silently produce an empty snapshot. Existing tests patch both paths and therefore conceal this error.

findings.title: Second-resolution filenames cause snapshot collisions
findings.evidence: Timestamp uses %Y%m%d_%H%M%S for both destination database (46) and manifest (70), without a unique suffix or retry. VACUUM INTO targets this same file at 52.
findings.trigger: Two calls create_snapshot occur within the same UTC second with an existing source database.
findings.impact: The second VACUUM INTO fails on the existing nonempty target, disrupting a valid backup request; concurrent writers may also contend for the manifest name.

findings.title: Software-key example certifies hardware-bound attestation
findings.evidence: ScittSigner::new generates an ed25519_dalek SigningKey with OsRng (30-34); sign accesses the in-process key (37-38). The final verdict prints hardware-bound certification at 231 and labels throughput hardware at 216.
findings.trigger: Run the example successfully on software signing alone.
findings.impact: Its output misrepresents software signature round trips as evidence of hardware-bound attestation, without any hardware key provider or hardware authorization step. The finding is limited to example claims.

findings.title: Receipt example accepts missing or malformed required fields
findings.evidence: Parser initializes epoch/hash/timestamp/strings to zero/empty (118-122), silently ignores mismatched types and invalid hash length (124-155), then returns Ok at 158.
findings.trigger: A validly signed CBOR map omits required fields or supplies wrong types.
findings.impact: Verification succeeds and returns default values rather than rejecting an invalid halt receipt; signature integrity alone does not establish the declared payload schema.

findings.title: Trace validator ignores sequence continuity and incomplete writes
findings.evidence: validateTransition names _currentSeq but never reads it; only checks parity/write boolean (19-32). isValidTrace [] returns true even when inWrite=true (36).
findings.trigger: Validate a single WriteBegin with odd seq, or WriteBegin 3 followed by WriteEnd 2, starting at (0,false).
findings.impact: The example validator accepts unfinished or regressing traces despite its seqlock validation wording. Its two concrete decide proofs do not cover these cases or prove runtime seqlock correctness.
